newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq rises in slim post-holiday trading.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq rises in slim post-holiday trading.

text.p: The Nasdaq Composite Index posted moderate gains in sluggish post-Christmas trading on the back of gains in the technology sector.

The Nasdaq Composite Index Thursday gained 6.94 or 0.54 percent to 1294.57. The Dow gained 24 points to unofficially close at 6546.68 in the slowest trading session so far in 1996. The long bond ended unchanged to yield 6.59 percent.
"There's no direction in the market since there's just nothing happening. There's not enough news to shift anything one way or another," one trader said.

Technology stocks rose as the Santa Claus rally continued. Intel Corp swelled 1-1/8 to 136-5/8, Dell Computer Corp rose 1-1/4 to 55-1/4 and Microsoft Corp gained 5/8 to 85-1/2. Cisco Systems was up 1-5/8 to 66-5/8.
WorldCom Inc, the most actively traded, and other long distance companies jumped on prospects of long-distance access charge reform. WorldCom gained 1 to 25 a share.

In other news, generic drug makers Watson Pharmaceuticals Inc and Royce Laboratories Inc agreed to merge. Watson, which gained 1-5/8 to 45-1/8 a share, sees the deal accretive to its 1997 earnings. Losing stocks beat gaining 2092 to 2028 on total volume of 392 million.
